chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in His decree and judgment, but He is Just in that.
And He said: Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and provides from Himself a great reward.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of Allah's justice in His decree and judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirming divine justice (*Adl*), emphasizing that Allah’s decree is perfectly fair and never unjust, even by the weight of an atom. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle that God’s judgment is rooted in absolute wisdom and mercy, multiplying good deeds as a sign of His generosity rather than mere retribution. It serves as a foundational proof for the belief that no soul is burdened beyond its capacity and that ultimate recompense is precisely calibrated to divine justice.
